sections.title: Getting started
paragraphs: Ferry shows Android devices as locations in Finder. It runs in the menu bar and has no Dock icon.
The first time Ferry opens, it starts a small helper that talks to your devices. The helper keeps running after you quit the menu, so devices stay in Finder.

groups.title: Turn on Ferry in Finder
steps: Click the Ferry icon in the menu bar.
Click **Open System Settings**.
In Login Items & Extensions, turn on Ferry under File Providers.

sections.title: Connect a NetAlly unit
paragraphs: For the LinkRunner 10G, EtherScope nXG and LinkRunner 100G.
steps: Connect a USB-C cable to the **USB-C port on the left side** of the unit and to the Mac.
On the unit: **Settings** (bottom of the Home screen) → **Connected devices** → **USB**.
Tap **Transfer files**.
sections.note: The device appears in Finder once it shares files.

sections.title: Connect another Android phone
paragraphs: Unlock the phone first. Its storage stays hidden while it is locked.

groups.title: Android 8 or 9
steps: Unlock the phone and connect it to the Mac with a USB cable. Its storage stays hidden while it is locked.
Pull down the notification shade and tap **USB charging this device**.
Tap **Transfer files**.

groups.title: Android 10 or newer
steps: Unlock the phone and connect it to the Mac with a USB cable. Its storage stays hidden while it is locked.
Pull down the notification shade and tap **Charging this device via USB**.
Under **USB preferences**, choose **File transfer**. Or open **Settings** → **Connected devices** → **USB**.

sections.title: USB debugging
paragraphs: With USB debugging on, Ferry serves the device over ADB, which is faster than file transfer and adds more tools. File transfer keeps working without it.

Ferry needs adb, from Google's Android platform tools. If it is missing, the menu shows **Install adb for more tools…** and the command to run: `brew install --cask android-platform-tools`. Click **Check again** once it is installed.
Menu names vary a little between phone makers. Look for Developer options and the USB debugging switch.

groups.title: NetAlly LinkRunner 10G, LinkRunner 100G or EtherScope nXG
steps: Ask NetAlly to enable ADB on the tester.
After that, on the tester: **Settings** → **System** → **About tester**. Tap **Build number** until developer mode is on.
Go to **Settings** → **System** → **Developer options** and turn on **USB debugging**.
With the USB-C cable connected to the Mac, turn **USB debugging** off and on again. The tester offers ADB only after this.
On the device, tick **Always allow from this computer** and tap **OK**.
groups.note: Once ADB is enabled, NetAlly testers also listen for ADB over the network on port 5555.

groups.title: Android 8 or 9
steps: Unlock the phone and connect it to the Mac with a USB cable. Its storage stays hidden while it is locked.
Open **Settings** → **System** → **About phone** and tap **Build number** until developer mode is on.
Open **Settings** → **System** → **Developer options** and turn on **USB debugging**.
On the device, tick **Always allow from this computer** and tap **OK**.

groups.title: Android 10 or newer
steps: Unlock the phone and connect it to the Mac with a USB cable. Its storage stays hidden while it is locked.
Open **Settings** → **About phone** and tap **Build number** until developer mode is on.
Open **Settings** → **System** → **Developer options** and turn on **USB debugging**.
On the device, tick **Always allow from this computer** and tap **Allow**.

link.title: How to turn on USB debugging

sections.title: Using Ferry in Finder
paragraphs: Each device appears in Finder's sidebar under Locations, and in every app's Open and Save dialogs. An SD card is a second location.
Double-click a file to open it. Ferry copies it to the Mac when you open it.
Drag files or folders between the device and the Mac to copy them. A half-copied file never appears under its real name.
Finder shows how far each copy has got, and the Ferry menu lists copies in progress under their device.

A package, such as an .rtfd document or an app, can't be copied to the device: compress it into a .zip first. Symbolic links and aliases can't be copied to the device either; Finder shows an error for them.

A folder on the device named like an app or a document package, such as Tool.app or Notes.rtfd, shows in Finder as an app or a document, because macOS goes by the name. It is read-only on the Mac, with everything in it: edit it on the device, or copy it to the Mac. Something put inside one stays on the Mac, and Finder shows an error for it. Saving one from a Mac app can leave a copy beside it, such as Notes 2.rtfd, which Finder marks with an error, with the edit only on the Mac: copy it to the Mac to keep it. A folder can't be renamed to such a name. To remove one, delete it on the device, or delete the folder that holds it; Finder may put that folder back once, so delete it again.
To see files added on the device while it is connected, choose **Refresh** in the Ferry menu.
Files over 4 GB copy to internal storage. Many SD cards cannot hold a file over 4 GB; Ferry shows an error instead of copying part of it.

groups.title: Delete
paragraphs: The device has no Trash. Finder offers **Delete Immediately**, and the file is removed from the device at once.

A folder is deleted with its contents only if Finder has shown everything in it, at every level, as it is now. If anything inside is new or changed on the device, or a folder inside was never opened, the whole folder stays and Finder puts it back. Delete it again to remove it. A folder nested more than 64 levels deep, or holding more than 100,000 items, also stays. A folder that holds a file whose name the Mac can't show stays too; delete it on the device.
A file the device changed since Finder last showed it is not deleted. Finder puts it back with the device's version.

groups.title: A file changed on both sides
paragraphs: If a file changed on the device after the Mac read it, Ferry keeps the device's version and saves yours beside it as **name (conflict from Mac)**.

groups.title: Free up space on the Mac
paragraphs: Control-click a file you opened and choose **Remove Download**. The file stays on the device.

definitions.term: Allow USB debugging on the device
definitions.detail: USB debugging is on, but this Mac is not allowed yet. On the device, tick **Always allow from this computer** and tap **OK** or **Allow**.
Only adb lists the device, and USB debugging is not allowed yet. Tap **OK** or **Allow** on the device.

definitions.term: Waiting for you to allow this Mac on…
definitions.detail: A device on your network is waiting for you to allow this Mac. Tap **Allow** on the device.
adb is not installed. Click **Copy**, run the command in Terminal, then click **Check again**.
adb is installed but its server is not answering. Click **Check again**.

Shows changes made on the device in Finder, mounts every device you ejected, and checks again a device that is not sharing files. While the menu is open, Ferry also checks for devices every 2 seconds.

Removes a ready device from Finder and releases it; it then shows **Ejected**. Changes that had not reached the device are saved to a folder on the Mac, and the menu offers **Reveal in Finder**. Deletes and renames that had not reached the device are dropped, so the device keeps those files under their old names.
Next to an ejected device: puts it back in Finder.
Opens this window.
Open at login, How to connect, Help and Remove Ferry.
Closes the menu. The helper keeps running, so devices stay in Finder.

sections.title: Tools over USB debugging
paragraphs: A device Ferry reaches over ADB (USB · ADB or Wi-Fi · ADB in the menu) shows Install App…, Screenshot and Record Screen under its name, and a Developer Tools menu. A device on file transfer shows More tools with USB debugging… instead.

groups.title: Install an app
paragraphs: Click Install App… and choose an .apk file, or drag one .apk onto the device in the menu. Ferry checks that the file is an Android app, copies it to the device and installs it, replacing an older version of the same app. The menu shows how far the copy has got, then says when the app is installed.

If the device refuses the app, the menu says why, for example that a newer version is installed or that the app needs a newer version of Android. Ferry removes its copy of the app from the device either way.

groups.title: Screenshots and screen recordings
paragraphs: Click Screenshot to save what the device's screen shows. Click Record Screen to record it, for up to three minutes; the menu shows how long it has been recording, and Stop ends it.

Ferry saves them where macOS saves its own screenshots (the Desktop, unless you chose another folder in the Screenshot app), named like macOS's own, such as Screenshot LinkRunner-100G 2026-11-18 at 17.09.27.png, and shows them in Finder. It never replaces a file. A recording waits on the device until Ferry has saved it, even if you quit Ferry meanwhile; Ferry then removes it from the device.

If Ferry can't save a recording, the menu shows Recording couldn't be saved: Choose Folder… saves it where you pick, and Discard deletes it from the device. Record Screen returns once it is saved or discarded. An ejected device keeps its recording until Ferry serves it again.
A device whose screen is off sends a black screenshot, and a recording of a screen that does not change has a single frame.

groups.title: Logcat
paragraphs: Choose Developer Tools, then Logcat…, to watch the device's log in a window of its own. Ferry keeps the newest 50,000 lines. Level shows lines at that level and above, and Filter shows the lines that contain your text, whatever its case. Pause freezes the window while lines keep arriving, and Resume catches up. Clear empties it.
Save… writes the lines that match the filters to a plain text file where you choose. The log stops when you close the window or the device goes away.

groups.title: Open a shell
paragraphs: Choose Developer Tools, then Open Shell, to open Terminal with a shell on the device (adb shell). Ferry needs adb for this, and says so if it can't find it. Nothing on the device changes unless you type a command that changes it.

groups.title: Forward a port
paragraphs: Choose Developer Tools, then Port Forwarding…, to send connections to a port on this Mac to a port on the device. Type the port on this Mac (1024 or higher) and the port on the device, then click Add. Remove ends a forward.
If the port on this Mac is already in use, the window shows adb's message. Ferry lists only the TCP forwards adb holds for this device.

groups.title: Device info
paragraphs: Choose Developer Tools, then Device Info…, to see the model, Android version, build, serial number, battery, IP addresses and storage the device reports. Ferry only reads them. Copy puts them on the clipboard.

groups.title: The device does not show up
steps: Try another cable. Some carry power only.
Unlock the device.
Turn on file transfer on the device.
Check that Ferry is on under File Providers in Login Items & Extensions.
Choose **Refresh** in the Ferry menu.

groups.title: Not sharing files
paragraphs: Unlock the device and choose Transfer files on it. You do not need to replug the cable.

link.title: How to turn on file transfer

groups.title: In use by another app
paragraphs: Quit Image Capture, Preview, Android File Transfer, MacDroid or OpenMTP, then click **Try Again**.

groups.title: The sidebar says "Ferry"
paragraphs: With one device location, macOS labels it with the app's name. This is normal.

groups.title: Unplugged during a copy
paragraphs: Plug the device back in and turn on file transfer. Finder finishes the copy when the device reconnects. A half-copied file never appears under its real name.

groups.title: Ferry's helper is not responding
paragraphs: If the menu says **Allow Ferry's helper** or **macOS can't find Ferry's helper**, click **Open System Settings** and turn on Ferry under Allow in the Background.
Otherwise, quit Ferry from the menu and open it again from Applications.

groups.title: Packages and app bundles can't be copied to the device
paragraphs: A package, such as an .rtfd or Keynote document, an app, a plug-in or a framework, is one item on the Mac but a folder on the device, so Ferry does not copy it. Control-click it, choose **Compress**, and copy the .zip instead.

groups.title: An app or script from the device does not open at once
paragraphs: Files copied from a device, and folders on it named like an app or a document package, are marked as downloaded, so macOS checks an app or script with Gatekeeper before it first opens, as it does for one from the internet.

sections.title: Privacy
paragraphs: Ferry has no telemetry, no analytics and no account, and sends nothing to any server. Your files go only between the device and your Mac. If you use ADB over Wi-Fi, Ferry talks to that device on your network and nowhere else.

sections.title: Uninstall
steps: In Ferry's Settings, click **Remove Ferry…** and confirm. Your devices disappear from Finder, Ferry's helper stops, and Ferry quits. Files on your devices are not touched.
Drag Ferry from Applications to the Trash.
